# Matrix operation {#sec-matrixOperationMath}

A reccurent theme in this first part of the book is that symbols and terms are the same but have different meaning. A variable is used in mathematics, in [statistics](@sec-variable), or a [function](@sec-functionMath) in mathematics and a [function](@sec-functionCoding) in programming. There are similarities but also nuanced meanings.

Above is an example of using mathematical notations (addition and equality) which differ from strict mathematical definition. Yet, they actually have a meaning, maybe not as rigorous as in mathematics.

In the previous a matrix is new kind of object, and it is worth defining what kind of operation can be done. The general idea is to generalize some of the arithmetic operation. What does it mean adding two matrices: Matrix 1 + Matrix 2 or multiplying two matrices Matrix 1 x matrix 2.

This chapter focuses element wise operation.

Let's reuse the example in [this chapter](@sec-matrixMath)

$$
A =
\begin{pmatrix}
    6 & 3 & 0.5 \\
    3 & 1 & 0 \\
    0 & 10 & 0 \\
    1 & 0 & 2
\end{pmatrix}
$$

amd multiply with 2

$$
2 \times A =
\begin{pmatrix}
    2 \times 6 & 2 \times 3 & 2 \times 0.5 \\
    2 \times 3 & 2 \times 1 & 2 \times 0 \\
    2 \times 0 & 2 \times 10 & 2 \times 0 \\
    2 \times 1 & 2 \times 0 & 2 \times 2
\end{pmatrix}
$$

This element-wise work (well-defined) when we combine a matrix with scalar or matrix of same dimension wi, the element-wise operation is mostly arithemetic operation for each element of the grid. All the propreties in traditional arithmetic operation with numbers naturally apply.

## Formal {.unnumbered}

Consider a number $x$, a matrix $A = \{a_{i,j}\}$ and $B = \{b_{i,j}\}$ of dimensions $m$ and $n$.

**The scalar operation are**

- Addition a scalar $x + A =  \{x + a_{i,j}\}$ for all i and j
- Multiplication a scalar $x \times A =  \{x \times a_{i,j}\}$ for all i and j
- Subtract a scalar $x - A =  \{x - a_{i,j}\}$ for all i and j
- Divide a scalar $ x / A =  \{x / a_{i,j}\}$ for all i and j

It should be obvious that $A + x$, $A - x$, $A \times x$ and $A / x$ are defined in the same manner

**Two matrices have the same dimensions**

- Addition a scalar $A  + B =  \{a_{i,j} + b_{i,j}\}$ for all i and j
- Subtract a scalar $ A - B =  \{a_{i,j} - b_{i,j}\}$ for all i and j
- Divide a scalar $ x / A =  \{x / a_{i,j}\}$ for all i and j


For a multiplication, a special notation is used
$A  \circ B =  \{a_{i,j} \times b_{i,j}\}$ and is called a Hadamard product.

The equivalent division, called Hadamard quotient, also exists and is noted: $A  \circ B^{-1} =  \{\frac{a_{i,j}}{b_{i,j}}\}$

\end{pmatrix}
$$
